claim: Testing effect: recall tests produced greater retention than restudy on delayed tests (2 days, 1 week); restudy did better at 5 minutes and raised confidence
quote_or_locator: Roediger & Karpicke 2006, Psychological Science 17(3) 249-255, abstract (OpenAlex): 'on the delayed tests, prior testing produced substantially greater retention than studying, even though repeated studying increased students' confidence'

claim: Meta-analysis of testing vs restudy: initial recall tests give larger testing benefits than recognition tests
quote_or_locator: Rowland 2014, Psychological Bulletin 140(6) 1432-1463, abstract (OpenAlex): 'initial recall tests yielding larger testing benefits than recognition tests'

claim: Distributed practice: the spacing gap that maximises retention grows with the retention interval (839 assessments, 317 experiments)
quote_or_locator: Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted & Rohrer 2006, Psychological Bulletin 132(3) 354-380, abstract (OpenAlex): 'the ISI producing maximal retention increased as retention interval increased'. [I] applying it to a next-day interview

claim: Short-term total sleep deprivation impairs cognition: effects from small and non-significant (reasoning accuracy) to large (lapses in simple attention)
quote_or_locator: Lim & Dinges 2010, Psychological Bulletin 136(3) 375-389, abstract (OpenAlex): 'from small and nonsignificant (reasoning accuracy: g = -0.125 ...) to large (lapses in simple attention: g = -0.776 ...)'. Total (<48 h) deprivation, not partial: [I] for a short night
